note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): also log the DuckDB file size after a dimension-growth append (it rewrites every table); the file may not shrink after drops without CHECKPOINT/VACUUM (general DuckDB knowledge, unverified).

**2026-10-10** — The four trial tests cover a round-trip that asserts the reopened rows and columns against both the generated source rows and the wide session, while the size, read-only open, and storage-version tests log their measurements. DuckDB measured 798,720 B, ZIP .ball 14,839 B, and Parquet 28,451 B; all measured DuckDB main-file sizes are whole 256 KiB blocks plus a 12 KiB header, so these ratios are not at-scale estimates. The writer-held read-only child open gets a conflicting lock and succeeds after writer disposal. The measured storage tag is v1.0.0+, the numeric header version is 64, and DuckDB is v1.5.5. The dimension-growth append grows the WAL, and CHECKPOINT does not shrink the main file. The child helper is the test-only tests/DataBall.TrialProbe console project. docs/ball-v3-trial.md answers the four db-06 questions. Deviation: the round-trip also compares with the wide session.

items.title: DataBall `.ball` v3 must be a DuckDB file
items.short_title: DataBall `.ball` v3 must be a DuckDB file

note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): a dimension-growth re-split rewrites every layout table; in a file-backed .ball the file may not shrink without CHECKPOINT/VACUUM (general DuckDB knowledge, unverified). Include that in the save path.

**2026-10-10** — From db-05 review (2026-10-09): read-only opens must also pass the in-process gate, since DuckDbStore (src/DataBall/DuckDbStore.cs:36-41) rejects a second DataBall on the same path regardless of mode, and every open writes meta (:51-56). db-05 DuckDB sizes are whole 256 KiB blocks plus a 12 KiB header, so measure size at a realistic row count before choosing the ZIP-fallback default. DuckDB's concurrency page mentions the Quack remote protocol (beta as of v1.5.2) for multi-process access; the snapshot recommendation assumes it is not used.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10: (1) snapshot publication for live readers moves to db-18. (2) A native .ball opens read-only by default; writable only on request. (3) Back-compat is dropped: ZIP .ball v1/v2 import and export are removed along with BallManifest, the v2 layout restore, and their tests and fixtures, since ZIP .ball was never deployed. .ball means a DuckDB file only. (4) The release is v2.0.0. (5) Compatibility stance from db-05 stands: keep the default storage version (64), record writer engine and storage versions, and claim no reader floor until tested.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec): SaveAsync parks the whole session even when a session filter is set; filters apply only to CSV/Parquet/archive export. Writable native open is an optional parameter: Open/OpenAsync(path, schemaPath = null, bool writable = false), meaningful only for a native .ball. ImportAsync of a native .ball stays (replace or append, one transaction) by ATTACHing it READ_ONLY and copying rows, metadata and config in; the CLI keeps its commands. Config lives inside the DuckDB file in a reserved, versioned table, not a separate file (table name and history semantics being settled).

**2026-10-10** — Owner 2026-10-10: config lives in a reserved table "_databall" inside the file: one row per config version (version INTEGER, ball_format = 3, config JSON text, duckdb_version, storage_version, written_at). A row is appended only when the merged config changes; the highest version is current. A config whose tables use "_databall" or "meta" is rejected. Open reads the latest row and writes nothing when read-only; a missing table or ball_format other than 3 fails clearly, and a ZIP file (PK magic) gets a message that 1.x ZIP .ball is unsupported.

**2026-10-10** — Owner 2026-10-10 (review round 1): the _databall duckdb_version and storage_version columns describe the last writer of the file. Every save stamps the copy's latest row with the saved file's real engine version and storage tag; no hard-coded fallback. Config history still grows only when the config changes. ImportAsync of a native .ball merges only Columns, Relationships, Tables and Metadata from the source config; the session keeps its own CSV and metadata-policy settings. Open still uses the full stored config.
**2026-10-10** — Owner 2026-10-10 (gate round): _databall.written_at on the latest row means last save, stamped with the engine and storage versions on every save.
**2026-10-10** — Owner 2026-10-10 (gate round): a read-only session saving to its own live path throws DataBallException (save to another path or open with writable: true) instead of a silent no-op.

items.title: DataBall must choose its store by size and take engine settings
items.short_title: DataBall must choose its store by size and take engine settings

note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): a dimension-growth append re-splits the whole session in one transaction, holding about three wide copies (_unsplit TEMP, base data, _wide TEMP) plus the new tables; TEMP tables stay in memory unless temp_directory is set. Measure this. Options: drop the two TEMP copies in UnsplitLayout/SplitIntoLayout, or grow declared-key dimensions in place (ALTER dim ADD COLUMN + key check; new dimension = CREATE + spine key column + one UPDATE).

**2026-10-10** — From db-06 review (2026-10-10): connection settings are built in DuckDbStore.BuildConnectionString; read-only is the first engine setting, so route engine settings through DuckDBConnectionStringBuilder in one place. Moving an in-memory session to a file can reuse DuckDbStore.SaveTo (COPY FROM DATABASE); same-path checks must be case-insensitive on Windows and macOS.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec interview): store choice by total input bytes vs EngineOptions.InMemoryMaxBytes, default 25% of available memory; engine settings in a new EngineOptions argument, not Config (never saved into a .ball); temp store under TempDirectory (default OS temp), deleted on dispose.

**2026-10-10** — Measured 2026-10-10 (db-07 relay, Codex implementer): 50k rows, one dimension-growth append, peak summed duckdb_memory().memory_usage_bytes sampled every 1 ms. In memory 135,231,488 → 117,473,280 bytes; temp file store 135,018,496 → 113,278,976 bytes. After removing the _wide copy and renaming _unsplit, the re-split still holds data + _cast (TEMP wide copy, in memory even on file stores) + the dropped old layout tables (kept until commit) + the new tables: more than two wide copies.

items.title: DataBall must return columnar and streaming reads
items.short_title: DataBall must return columnar and streaming reads

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): ReadColumns returns T[] Values plus bool[]? Nulls per column (Nulls null when the column has none).

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-08 relay review): (1) a column created from an all-null handler batch with no config type is widened automatically when a later batch brings its first typed value (ALTER ... TYPE in that batch's transaction; safe because every stored value is NULL). (2) ReadColumns uses a complete read-side type map, separate from import typing: SMALLINT/TINYINT/UTINYINT/USMALLINT -> int, UINTEGER -> long, DECIMAL/UBIGINT/HUGEINT -> double, everything else -> string; it never throws on type, and any remaining error names the column.

items.title: DataBall must attach Parquet and hive inputs as views
items.short_title: DataBall must attach Parquet and hive inputs as views

note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): UnsplitLayout/DropDataRelation drop and copy physical tables, assuming the session owns them. Growth on an attached Parquet source would copy data in, defeating no-copy. Decide whether growth on attached sources is allowed.
**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec interview): a write to a view-backed session copies the view in on first write; SaveAsync embeds by default, link is opt-in.

**2026-10-10** — From db-07 relay (2026-10-10): OpenAsync picks a temp-file store by input size before reading. A view-backed Parquet/hive open copies nothing, so it should not create a temp file at open, but materialize-on-first-write copies the whole source, so the size rule should apply there (or the store be chosen by source size anyway). Decide which. Hive directories are sized by db-07's resolver (directories walked).

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-09 spec review): (1) configured metadata fields are extracted for Parquet on both a view and ImportAsync (file and hive dir), at the same point as the CSV path; MergeOrAppend's internal hand-off does not extract. (2) The db-07 store choice stays at open, by source size (ResolveStore walks hive directories). Spec review also found that OpenAsync rejects directories (File.Exists), so Open must accept hive Parquet directories.

**2026-10-10** — Spec amended 2026-10-10 (orchestrator, after the implementer stopped on a scope gap): DataBall.RowBuilder.cs added to Files. InitializeRow materializes the view in its own transaction (a failed InitializeRow leaves the view); CommitRow then runs on a table-backed session unchanged. Test 7 (ViewSession_FailedWrite_StaysView) covers a failing InitializeRow, not a failing CommitRow after a successful InitializeRow.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-09 review round 1): (1) Option C: a new default metadataPolicy 'liftConstant' for every format. A configured metadata field with one distinct non-null value moves to Metadata (nulls allowed, as requireConstant does); a field that varies stays a column and never throws. requireConstant, bounce and first stay as explicit opt-ins. This widens the Must-not-change exception: CSV and Parquet imports with a varying configured field now load (Lot as a column) instead of throwing. (2) Registered handlers keep precedence for files: Open asks FindHandler first and takes the Parquet view path only when no handler claims the file or it delegates to generic import.

items.title: DataBall must score format detection and explain it
items.short_title: DataBall must score format detection and explain it

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec interview): add Score(FileProbe) to IFormatHandler and keep CanHandle (default Score maps it to 1/0); JSON file types load from ~/.databall/types/, then ./databall/types/, then RegisterFileType; a later origin overrides the same id+version; origins are reported.

**2026-10-10** — From db-09 relay (2026-10-10): Open checks registered handlers first for files, then routes .parquet files and directories containing *.parquet to the built-in view path. Scored detection must make the built-in Parquet/hive path one scored candidate against handlers, and the view path must take the merged overlay config (a parquetColumns type's Overlay has to reach the view; compute HasLayoutConfig after the overlay merge).

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-10 spec review): (1) built-in paths (native .ball, Parquet view, generic CSV/archive import) are a fallback, not scored candidates: a scored candidate always wins; detect --explain reports the built-in as the Generic outcome with a reason (consistent with db-09 handler precedence). (2) Keep both type folders (~/.databall/types and ./databall/types); restricting folder-loaded types once types can carry SQL is a db-13 item. Spec review also moved detection before session construction, scored CustomCsvHandler at 0.6, and switched parquetColumns to DESCRIBE (parquet_schema lists the root and nested children).

**2026-10-10** — Spec amended 2026-10-10 (orchestrator, after the implementer stopped on a spec conflict): the 64 KiB read limit applies to FileProbe and every new scorer (JSON types, lab handlers' new Score), not to a legacy handler's CanHandle. The default Score keeps giving CanHandle the full file stream at position 0, exactly as FindHandler does today, so third-party handlers behave unchanged. Must not change's 'no file is read past 64 KiB' means DataBall's own detection reads.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (after the implementer stopped on undefined JSON syntax): lineMatches is exactly one of {line, regex} or {firstLines, regex}; columnCount is {min, max} (inclusive, either optional); headerContainsAll takes literal names only (aliases come with db-12 sources). The full syntax table for all eight conditions is now in the Files section.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-10 review round 1): (1) LabHandlers.RegisterDefaults is idempotent: it skips a handler type already registered (duplicates registered by hand still tie as ambiguous). (2) Config precedence in Open: defaults, then the winning type's overlay, then the host's schemaPath, so an explicit host schema overrides a detected type. This replaces spec step 3's order.

items.title: DataBall must open many files into one session
items.short_title: DataBall must open many files into one session

note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): each later file bringing a new per-source metadata key triggers another full re-split (cost ~ files x session size). Stage all sources first and split once, or use in-place dimension growth (see db-07 note). Also: a declared key column that arrives as metadata (constant in file 1) still throws 'tables.X.key ... is not in the data' in TableLayout.Build; the run key must handle this.

**2026-10-09** — From db-02 review (2026-10-08): layout physical types are fixed at first import and the re-split casts incoming data to existing types, which conflicts with db-11's planned numeric-widening schema merge. Decide how widening applies to layout sessions.

**2026-10-10** — From db-06 review (2026-10-10): native .ball import ATTACHes the source READ_ONLY for one import transaction (deferred DETACH in the store transaction) and does not consult the in-process open-file gate. Many files in one session needs a session-lifetime attachment registry through that gate, and a policy for merging several stored _databall configs (db-06 import merges only columns, relationships, tables and metadata).

**2026-10-10** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (spec interview): BCL-only globbing (wildcards in the last segment, Recursive option); built-in "source" dimension (_source_file, _source_hash, _source_type, per-source meta columns), "meta" keeps only values constant across sources, wide sessions carry lineage columns directly; every file-opened session has lineage, even one file; widening in layout sessions ALTERs the owning physical column.

**2026-10-10** — From db-07 relay (2026-10-10): the re-split peak fell only ~13-16% (135 → 117 MB at 50k rows); _cast is a TEMP wide copy that stays in memory on file-backed stores, and dropped layout tables are kept until commit. In-place dimension growth (or a non-TEMP _cast on file stores) is still the lever. The store threshold uses on-disk bytes, which understate memory for compressed archives and Parquet. Use db-07's store resolver over the expanded input list rather than adding a new call site.

**2026-10-10** — From db-07 gate (2026-10-10): EngineOptions.ResolveStore walks directories with Directory.EnumerateFiles(..., AllDirectories), which can throw a raw UnauthorizedAccessException on an unreadable subdirectory. Wrap it in DataBallException when many-file open reuses the resolver.

**2026-10-10** — From db-08 relay (2026-10-10): db-08 drains handlers in 10,000-row batches and widens a column created from an all-null batch when a later batch brings a typed value; db-11's numeric widening (INTEGER->BIGINT->DOUBLE) should use the same in-place path for later sources. Handler opens on a layout session split once after all batches (db-08); keep that when staging many sources.

**2026-10-10** — From db-09 relay (2026-10-10): (1) The new default metadataPolicy 'liftConstant' (lift a field with one distinct value to Metadata, else keep it as a column, never throw) is the single-source case of db-11's three levels: constant everywhere -> Metadata, constant within a source but varying across sources -> source column, varying within a source -> row column. Extend it; don't replace it. (2) Open treats any directory with *.parquet at any depth as one hive source, viewed with one read_parquet glob without union_by_name; directory expansion must decide which directories stay one hive source. (3) IsViewBacked must not mistake a source-dimension view of data for an external Parquet view; Parquet views stay single-source. (4) A wide CSV append and a Parquet append reconcile differing stored metadata differently; unify when wide schema handling moves to staging.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 relay (2026-10-10): Detect per expanded file builds a FileProbe (db-10 makes ParquetColumns lazy, so only parquetColumns conditions pay the DuckDB DESCRIBE); a hive Open walks the tree in OpenAsync, Detect and ResolveStore — walk once when expanding inputs. Route each file from DetectionReport.BuiltInPath (an enum after db-10).

**2026-10-11** — Split 2026-10-10 (owner): db-11 is now the many-input core; lineage moved to db-22, schema merge and widening to db-23, bad-file policy, Skipped report and CLI multi-input to db-24, native .ball sources to db-25 (all in group 'Many-file open'). Model note: Claude-only relay; implementer Sonnet 5.5 high, Haiku 5.5 high subagents for well-scoped pieces.

**2026-10-11** — From db-22 interview (owner, 2026-10-10): lineage is normalized. Rows carry _source_key and a built-in source table holds path/sha256/type/bytes/modified/added. Per-source metadata that varies across sources therefore becomes columns of the source table, not of data; the three-level liftConstant rule references source. OpenReport.Sources reuses db.Sources.

**2026-10-11** — From db-22 relay (2026-10-11): (1) db-22 remaps source rows in two places with a fixed column list (RemapStagingSources for MergeOrAppend, BringNativeSources for .ball import); per-source metadata columns on source would be dropped. Replace both with one SQL remap (INSERT INTO source SELECT * REPLACE (source_key + offset AS source_key) ...), with the merge hand-off carrying the other session's source table. (2) ImportFromFunction stages, keys (AttachSourceKey) and merges in one call; stage-all-then-split-once needs stage+key separated from the merge. (3) A hive directory is one source whose sha256 hashes its sorted per-file hashes; type records the detected BuiltInPath (a Parquet copy shows ParquetView).

items.title: DataBall CSV must handle preambles, trailers and strict casts
items.short_title: DataBall CSV must handle preambles, trailers and strict casts

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): strict casts apply only to columns with a declared type; undeclared columns keep DuckDB inference.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 relay (2026-10-10): (1) a delegating JSON type that wins on a non-.csv text feed (.txt/.tsv/.dat) cannot open, because the built-in route still comes from DetectFormat's extension table; when CSV settings live in a type's config, let the winning type choose the CSV reader regardless of extension. (2) FileProbe.HeaderFields is line 0 with the sniffed delimiter and fileNameRegex named groups are not retained;  and preambles must expose captures and a post-preamble header to conditions. (3) Precedence is defaults < type overlay < host schemaPath (owner, 2026-10-10).

items.title: DataBall must apply declarative transforms from config
items.short_title: DataBall must apply declarative transforms from config

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): transforms live in Config (and a file type's config), run per source on staging at import before the merge, and travel in the .ball.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 spec review (owner, 2026-10-10): JSON file types auto-load from ~/.databall/types and ./databall/types (working directory). Once a type's config can carry transforms (SQL expressions), a type loaded from a folder must not carry transforms or combine unless the host registers it explicitly (RegisterFileType or CLI --types); opening a file in an untrusted working directory must not run its SQL.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 relay (2026-10-10): to restrict folder-loaded types, record an origin kind (HomeFolder/LocalFolder/Registered) set in LoadFolders and RegisterFileType (a path alone can't tell them apart). A type file with the same id and a different version coexists with the old one, so an upgraded type left next to the old file is ambiguous. Decide whether one invalid file in ~/.databall/types should fail every Open in the process (LoadFolders throws and retries per call). db-10 makes unknown top-level keys in a type file invalid.

items.short_title: DataBall must join, dedupe and aggregate across sources

items.title: DataBall export must support profiles and content splits
items.short_title: DataBall export must support profiles and content splits

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): four bundled profiles plus exportProfiles in Config; staging at <out>/.databall-staging/<id>/; manifest at <out>/_manifest/<id>.json.

**2026-10-11** — From db-22 interview (owner, 2026-10-10): CSV/Parquet/archive/hive exports resolve _source_key into _source_file and _source_type through a join on source. Export profiles and splits must keep that join, and a split by source should use the resolved columns.

**2026-10-11** — From db-22 relay (2026-10-11): ResolveSourceSql replaces data columns named _source_file/_source_type (host writes of _source* are now rejected; imports rename them to origin_*) and skips lineage when a projection omits _source_key. Export profiles inherit both rules.

items.title: DataBall API must have one clear way in and out
items.short_title: DataBall API must have one clear way in and out

note_records.text: **2026-10-09** — From db-02 architecture review (2026-10-09): three separate ways restore in-memory state after a failed write: TakeSnapshot/RestoreSnapshot (RunImport, OnWideData), the wide-Bounce expected-types copy (DataBall.cs ~313), and CommitRow's ForgetUnstoredColumnTypes. The store also restores Layout and reloads metadata itself. Root cause: wide-session EnsureColumn runs ALTER outside the write transaction. Move CommitRow column creation into the store write transaction, then CommitRow and Bounce can use TakeSnapshot/RestoreSnapshot.

**2026-10-10** — From db-06 review (2026-10-10): there are now four ways into a .ball: Open (native, read-only by default), new DataBall(databasePath: x.ball) (native, writable, writes _databall on open), ImportAsync (copy), and the public statics ImportManager.ImportFromBall / ExportManager.ExportToBall (thin wrappers). OpenAsync gained bool writable before the CancellationToken (source-breaking for OpenAsync(path, null, ct)). The stored config holds the full merged defaults, so later default changes never reach existing files. Fold these into the one-way-in/out API.

**2026-10-10** — Owner decision 2026-10-10 (spec interview): remove the old entry points outright in v2.0.0 (no [Obsolete] shims). Still open: whether the stored _databall config keeps full merged defaults or only the overlay (step 1 of Implement).

**2026-10-10** — From db-07 relay (2026-10-10): db-07 added EngineOptions? engine to Open (after writable), OpenAsync (before the CancellationToken, so positional OpenAsync(path, schema, writable, ct) no longer compiles) and as the 4th public ctor parameter, plus public EngineOptions/StoreMode and CLI --memory-limit/--threads/--temp-dir/--store. Fold engine into OpenOptions.Engine. With an explicit databasePath, EngineOptions.Store is ignored; a create-only ctor could reject databasePath with Store = File.

**2026-10-10** — From db-08 relay (2026-10-10): ReadRowsAsync streams on the session's single connection, so db-08 guards every store command while a stream is open; fold that guard (or a dedicated stream connection, which would not see TEMP objects or the open transaction) into the one-way-out API. Query(sql) can run DML and is not covered by the write guard. ReadColumns and ReadRowsAsync run synchronously on the caller's thread (Open escapes the sync context with Task.Run; these do not): decide whether the folded read API offloads for UI hosts. Plots want double[]: consider ColumnData.ToDoubleArray() or a read option that casts numeric columns to DOUBLE in SQL.

**2026-10-10** — From db-09 relay (2026-10-10): materialize-before-write sits at several call sites (store AddRow/AddRows, SaveTo in-place, RunImport, OnWideData, wide Bounce, InitializeRow); fold into one write-transaction entry point with the rollback unification. Decide whether SaveOptions.Link governs an in-place save of a linked .ball (today it embeds in place) and whether link paths may be relative to the .ball.

**2026-10-10** — From db-09 gate (2026-10-10): (1) the cached IsViewBacked flag goes stale after raw DDL on "data" through Query (every later write then fails); fold it into the Query write guard, or re-check DataIsView() in MaterializeView. (2) Under explicit requireConstant a wide Parquet append with a differing value demotes the field while the same CSV append throws (ImportParquetWithMetadata skips reconciled fields). (3) .ball files saved before db-09 store metadataPolicy requireConstant in their merged config and keep it; part of the stored-config decision.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 relay (2026-10-10): public surface db-10 adds, to fold: IFormatHandler defaults Name/Priority/MinScore/Score/Overlay; FileProbe's public constructor does IO plus a DuckDB query (consider a factory); DetectionReport.Winner exposes the internal JsonFileType (Parse throws NotSupportedException); Overlay returns a mutable Config shared across opens; FileTypeInfo lives in namespace squalor.DataBall.FileTypes, which shares its name with the DataBall.FileTypes property; JSON type Name is the id without version. The CLI's import/query/export use ImportAsync, not Open, so detect --types predicts a route databall import does not take.

**2026-10-10** — From db-10 gate (2026-10-10): DataBall.csproj grants InternalsVisibleTo to the shipped DataBall.Handlers package for LabHandlers.RegisterDefaults' idempotence (internal RegisterHandlerIfMissing, atomic under HandlerGate). Fold it into the registry API (e.g. a public RegisterHandler overload or option that skips an already-registered type) or pin Handlers to an exact DataBall version, so the two packages cannot skew at runtime (MissingMethodException if a newer DataBall renames the internal method).
**2026-10-11** — From db-22 interview (owner, 2026-10-10): db-22 adds public IReadOnlyList<SourceInfo> Sources; fold it into the read API.

items.title: DataBall must publish closed .ball snapshots for live readers
items.short_title: Live-reader .ball snapshots

note_records.text: **2026-10-10** — Owner 2026-10-10: split out of db-06. A writer publishes a separate, completed, closed snapshot generation that readers open read-only; direct cross-process reads of the active capture file are not promised (db-05 measured a conflicting lock). Covers snapshot creation, publication, cadence, and consistency under concurrent capture (docs/ball-v3-trial.md).

**2026-10-10** — From db-06 review (2026-10-10): DuckDbStore.SaveTo (temp file, COPY FROM DATABASE, File.Move) is the publication primitive. Snapshot publication needs a unique temp name per save, a check against the in-process open-file gate on the target, and a plan for Windows, where a reader holding the target blocks the replace (POSIX readers keep the old inode). Saving to the session's own path is only a CHECKPOINT and does not compact.

**2026-10-10** — From db-06 architect gate (2026-10-10): SaveTo holds the process-wide FileGate for the whole copy (ATTACH, COPY FROM DATABASE, DETACH, File.Move), so every file-backed open, dispose or save in the process waits on it. Frequent snapshot publication should reserve the target in OpenFiles under the gate and release the gate during I/O.

**2026-10-10** — From db-09 relay (2026-10-10): for a view-backed session every embed SaveTo re-reads and re-encodes the whole external Parquet while holding the process-wide FileGate. Snapshot publication of a view-backed session should link, or materialize the live session once before the first snapshot.

note_records.text: **2026-10-11** — Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (db-22 interview): (1) normalized lineage: an always-present source table (source_key BIGINT 1..n in import order, path, sha256, type, bytes, modified_utc, added_utc) and one _source_key per row in wide and layout sessions; data shows the key, not path/hash/type; (2) full SHA-256 at open; (3) capture rows NULL key; pre-db-22 .ball files have no source table; (4) CSV/Parquet/archive/hive exports resolve the key to _source_file and _source_type; .ball keeps the normalized tables; (5) db.Sources (SourceInfo) read API; (6) names as listed, source and _source* reserved; (7) Claude-only relay, Sonnet 5.5 high implementer, Haiku 5.5 high subagent for test and export churn, Opus medium reviewer, architect and gate; owner signs off the spec before the relay.

**2026-10-11** — Owner decisions 2026-10-11 (db-22 review round 1): (1) _source* names are rejected by every public write (AddRow, AddRows, InitializeRow initial values, ModifyField, AddColumn, RemoveColumn) and by tables claims in config; internal paths unaffected. (2) The source table stays lazy (created on first import); exports, db.Sources and the CLI handle its absence, and a session with the key column but no source table exports NULL lineage columns, never the raw key. (3) A hive directory's sha256 is the SHA-256 over its sorted (relative path, file SHA-256) list. (4) Bounce/Squish DISTINCT ignores _source_key and collapses identical rows across files, keeping the lowest key. (5) On import, incoming _source_file/_source_type columns are renamed to origin_source_file/origin_source_type; any other incoming _source* column throws. (6) SourceInfo becomes a sealed class with get/init properties and an internal constructor. Also acknowledged: the BaseTables test helper excludes the built-in source table.

goals:
DataBall is the session engine of the squalor semiconductor suite, co-developed with `squalor-xyz/suite` and shared by its hosts. One run lives in one DataBall: in-memory DuckDB by default, file-backed on request. It sits behind the wide `"data"` relation plus `"meta"`, and is parked to a file and reopened from one.

- **ATE spirit:** sequential test-executive tables; DuckDB is the only SQL engine; interchange is CSV / Parquet / zip-tar.gz; from v2.0.0 a `.ball` is the native DuckDB session file.
- **One way in:** `Open` detects the format and hands lab dialects to an `IFormatHandler`. Parsers never go in the store.
- **Schema from config, not sniffing:** types, units, roles, and metadata fields come from the default profile plus overlay config. A config-declared multi-table layout (`tables`) sits behind the same `"data"` view, so readers never see the split.
- **Now:** `v1.3.0` is the last 1.x release (db-04, 2026-10-09). The planned v1.4.0 was renumbered v2.0.0 on 2026-10-10 because `.ball` becomes a DuckDB file and ZIP `.ball` support is dropped. The db-05 trial is done; db-06 is next.
- **Next, v2.0.0 (planned, not shipped; suite `docs/databall-v1.4-alignment.md`, written as v1.4.0):** one session holds one or more runs through a run/source dimension; `.ball` becomes a DuckDB file and ZIP `.ball` v1/v2 import and export are removed (never deployed); the store is in-memory or file-backed by size, so data larger than RAM works; hosts read typed columns or streamed rows with projection and filter pushdown; `Open` scores detection and opens many files; declarative transforms, combine ops, and export profiles fold in from the Conflux spec (db-05–db-17, snowflake `parent` db-03 included).

License: **Apache-2.0** as of 1.1.0 (1.0.0 was MPL-2.0).
non_goals: Hierarchical `DataFile`/`DataGroup`/`DataSweep` as an **object model** (the storage layout may be multi-table via config `tables`; the API stays rows + `"data"`), Polars, DataFrame, SQLite, matrix Bounce, MotherDuck, Spectre.Console, Coverlet, GB-scale fixtures in CI, nuget.org listing, watch folders, a TUI, a separate pipeline product (Conflux folds into DataBall).
